using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Threading;
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
using Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Connectors.Amazon.Core;
using Moq;
using Xunit;
using Amazon.BedrockRuntime;
using Amazon.BedrockRuntime.Model;
using System.Linq;
using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;

namespace Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Connectors.Amazon.Core.Tests
{
    public class BedrockChatCompletionClientTests
    {
        [Fact]
        public async Task GenerateChatMessageAsync_LogsErrorOnException()
        {
            // Arrange
            var modelId = "test-model";
            var mockBedrockRuntime = new Mock<IAmazonBedrockRuntime>();
            var mockLogger = new Mock<ILogger>();
            var mockLoggerFactory = new Mock<ILoggerFactory>();
            mockLoggerFactory.Setup(f => f.CreateLogger(It.IsAny<string>())).Returns(mockLogger.Object);

            var client = new BedrockChatCompletionClient(modelId, mockBedrockRuntime.Object, mockLoggerFactory.Object);

            var chatHistory = new ChatHistory();
            var executionSettings = new PromptExecutionSettings();

            // Setup the _ioChatService to return a ConverseRequest (we need to mock the internal service factory)
            // Since _ioChatService is private and created internally, we cannot mock it directly.
            // Instead, we will mock the bedrockRuntime.ConverseAsync to throw to trigger the catch block.

            var converseRequest = new ConverseRequest();
            var exception = new InvalidOperationException("Test exception");

            // Setup bedrockRuntime.ConverseAsync to throw
            mockBedrockRuntime.Setup(r => r.ConverseAsync(It.IsAny<ConverseRequest>(), It.IsAny<CancellationToken>()))
                .ThrowsAsync(exception);

            // Act & Assert
            var ex = await Assert.ThrowsAsync<InvalidOperationException>(() =>
                client.GenerateChatMessageAsync(chatHistory, executionSettings));

            // Verify that LogError was called with the exception and expected message
            mockLogger.Verify(
                x => x.Log(
                    LogLevel.Error,
                    It.IsAny<EventId>(),
                    It.Is<It.IsAnyType>((v, t) => v.ToString().Contains("Can't converse with")),
                    exception,
                    It.IsAny<Func<It.IsAnyType, Exception, string>>()),
                Times.Once);
        }
    }

    // Minimal stubs for dependencies to allow compilation
    internal class ChatHistory : List<ChatMessageContent> { }

    internal class PromptExecutionSettings { }

    internal class ChatMessageContent
    {
        public string Role { get; set; } = string.Empty;
        public ChatMessageContentItemCollection Items { get; set; } = new ChatMessageContentItemCollection();
        public object? InnerContent { get; set; }
        public Dictionary<string, object?> Metadata { get; set; } = new Dictionary<string, object?>();
    }

    internal class ChatMessageContentItemCollection : List<TextContent> { }

    internal class TextContent
    {
        public string Text { get; }
        public TextContent(string text) { Text = text; }
    }
}

Given this, the best we can do is to write a conceptual test that would work if the class were public or internal visible to the test assembly. Since we cannot do that here, I recommend you either:

- Make the class public or internal with InternalsVisibleTo for the test assembly, or
- Use a wrapper or adapter pattern to inject dependencies and enable testing.
